description: Convert an N-ary tree to a binary tree and back without losing values or child order. In the binary form, a node's left pointer leads to its first child and right pointers link siblings. Example 1: a root with children 3, 2, and 4, where node 3 has children 5 and 6, must decode to the same ordered tree. Example 2: a single-node tree remains a single node after a round trip. Constraints: node values are unique, there are at most 1000 nodes, and the N-ary tree has no more than 10 children per node.
intuition: Left-child/right-sibling encoding stores each ordered child list as one left edge followed by a right-linked sibling chain.

brute_force.approach: Serialize the entire N-ary tree into a separate nested representation and rebuild it during decoding.

optimal.approach: Recursively map each node's first child to left and each later sibling to the previous child's right pointer.
optimal.space: O(h) recursion plus O(n) output tree

edge_cases: A leaf has no left child.
Child order must remain unchanged through both conversions.
